# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Cost-reduction opportunity (if `cost`/`latency`/`num_messages` is a declared objective,
      run `detect_loop_patterns.py --run-dir $R --tag $BEST --split val` — free, no extra
      eval — and check its `by_tool` map for a same-tool-called-N-times-in-a-row pattern. A
      hit names the exact tool + repeat count: propose a composite/bulk tool (capability
      `tools`), a bundled script entrypoint (`skills-package`), or upfront-batched
      instructions (`prompt`/`system-prompt`) that replace the N calls with one. No hit
      (or cost/latency not a declared objective): say so plainly, do not leave this blank):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — judge-parity contract validator as a structural gate + knowledge fixes for the 6 failure clusters
- Changes I made (1 line/edit; file + cluster):
  1. NEW `epic-decompose/scripts/validate_decomposition.py` — bundled validator checking body sections, component vocabulary, Rule 11 docs-last closure, priority inheritance (clusters A/C/D/E).
  2. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8c (+Step 0): validator run is a precondition of the `decompose_complete` sentinel (clusters A/C/D/E).
  3. `prompts/review-agent.md` new Step 1.7: reviewer runs the validator, every VIOLATION becomes an issues entry + zeroed criterion (clusters A/C/D/E).
  4. `prompts/revise-agent.md` Step 2 + Step 4: mechanical correction playbook per violation type + re-run until OK (clusters A/C/D/E).
  5. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 2: component values verbatim from the canonical list, never invented/combined; span noted, not invented (cluster D).
  6. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 4: redundant-HLR consolidation rule with worked example (cluster B).
  7. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 3: presentation-mode split = scope duplication, major (cluster B).
  8. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 7: external schedule constraints are not ACs — Risks/Health Warnings; worked example (cluster F).
  9. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 6: soft-AC scan → minor issue "move to Risks/Notes" (cluster F).
  10. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8b: the four body-section headings are literal for every epic incl. docs-authoring; "Content Outline" is not "Scope" (cluster A).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - (1)-(4) fix the 4 mechanically-decidable failing trials: case-020 t1 (artifact_contract hard gate, reward 0 → ~1.0), case-018 t2 (dq 4→5), case-013 t2 (component gate −0.1), case-024 t1 (Rule 11 gate −0.1). Safe because the script was verified against ALL 33 trial artifacts: it flags exactly those 4 trials (+ case-018 t0's identical latent priority defect, whose remedy is the t2 grader's own stated fix) and exits 0 on every other trial — so on passing tasks the gate is a no-op. The review→revise mapping only adds issues when a violation exists, and the zeroing instruction keeps review_discipline arithmetic consistent.
  - (5) fixes case-013 t2's invented 'Model Serving Stack': the OLD prompt's fallback example itself modeled inventing a non-canonical name — the rewrite makes verbatim-from-list the only path. Safe: all passing trials already comply.
  - (6)+(7) fix case-015 t1/t2 (dq 3/5, both trials): the traces show the agent SAW the HLR overlap and split anyway, and the review endorsed it 14/14; the passing trial t0 of the same task already consolidates citing Step 4 — the rule makes the consistent behavior the only permitted one. Safe: verified no passing decomposition splits two presentation modes of one surface (they split by component/binary/work-type/repo).
  - (8)+(9) fix case-013 t0's dq-4 "one minor gap" (schedule-risk note as AC). Safe: grep-verified no passing trial carries a schedule-note AC.
  - (10) fixes the exact case-020 t1 heading rename; safe: surveyed every docs epic in all 33 trials — only the failing trial deviated.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist (iteration 1 on the seed). Refuted hypotheses: none yet (rejected.jsonl is empty).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none identified beyond the six fixed; the two dq-level residual risks are (a) grader inconsistency on priority inheritance (t0 passed with the defect t2 was dinged for — my check enforces the rule uniformly, which should help both), and (b) the redundancy judgment itself remains LLM-graded — if the grader ever rewards the split shape, edit 6/7 would need rescoping (watch case-015's per-trial grades).
- Refuted hypotheses: n/a (first iteration).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration; val 0.918 baseline, 5 flaky tasks all diagnosed).
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective this run; detect_loop_patterns not applicable. The validator adds ~2 cheap local Bash calls per case (no model tokens).
- Focus next iteration: read the gate RESULT per-task. If case-015 stays split (edit 6/7 insufficient for the reader tier), consider pushing the consolidation check into the validator as a heuristic (two same-team Implementation epics whose HLR Traceability sets overlap AND whose titles share a surface keyword) — only if the LLM rule under-triggers. If any passing task regressed, check first whether the validator fired on it (it shouldn't — corpus-verified) and whether the review-zeroing interacted badly with review_discipline.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.982 Δ=+0.064 · fixed={case-015-redundant-hlrs} · broke={—} · unresolved={case-013-human-process-gates, case-014-tech-preview-foundation, case-018-cross-strategy-dependency, case-020-hardware-dependent-investigation, case-024-real-default-vector-store} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.982 Δ=+0.064 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — consistency fixes for the 3 remaining flaky trials: Rule-10 validator check, architecture_claims calibration, soft-AC availability boundary
- Changes I made (1 line/edit; file + cluster):
  1. `scripts/validate_decomposition.py` — NEW check 5: implementation-type parallelism (Rules 7/8/10, judge parity) (cluster A / case-013 t0).
  2. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Rule 10 — no component-scope or artifact-dependency exemption; coupling → AC on the consuming epic (cluster A).
  3. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Rule 13 — build-pipeline outputs consumed as content (attestations, SBOMs, provenance) are AC gates, not edges (cluster A).
  4. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8c — validator description now includes the parallel check + fix recipe (cluster A).
  5. `prompts/review-agent.md` Step 1.7 — parallel-edge violation → critical / DAG Coherence mapping (cluster A).
  6. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 2 — ANY-component scope, attestations-as-content carve-out, and no missing-edge report for config references (cluster A).
  7. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — parallel-edge correction playbook entry (cluster A).
  8. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 6 signal 9 row + scoring note — a strategy premise about what a component IS (maturity state, surfaces, deployment model) is an architecture claim; +1 cites the context file; 0 only when no context covers the components (cluster B / case-014 t1).
  9. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 5 — architecture_claims calibration check against .context, minor issue (cluster B).
  10. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — architecture_claims re-scoring recipe against .context (cluster B).
  11. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 7 — soft-AC boundary broadened from schedule constraints to ALL externally-controlled preconditions (schedule + availability: procurement, node allocation, partner-lab access), with worked example (cluster C / case-020 t0).
  12. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 6 — soft-AC scan broadened to availability preconditions; "the epic's work includes securing the access" explicitly not a defense; deliverable-condition ACs using "available" explicitly valid (cluster C).
  13. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — NEW correction "misfiled soft AC → move to Risks/Notes + replace with a deliverable AC" (the review's move-to-Risks correction previously had no playbook entry) (cluster C).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - (1)-(7) fix case-013 t0's −0.1 implementation_type_rules: the validator (precondition of decompose_complete, wired through review 1.7 + revise) now mechanically forbids the konflux-onboarding→general edge the t0 review rationalized past — expected 0.9→1.0 on that trial class. Safe: corpus-verified the check flags EXACTLY case-013 t0 across all 33 trials (case-020's konflux epics with the no-edge shape pass cleanly, and that shape is dq-grader-PRAISED); judge parity means it can only fire where the external judge already fails.
  - (8)-(10) fix case-014 t1's dq-4: the failing trial's all-0 "no architecture claims" scoring becomes +1-with-context-citation (the passing siblings' exact shape). Safe: the rule fires only when a strategy premise asserts a component state/maturity — the all-0 PASSING trials (case-015/017/019) have no such premises (grep-verified), so their 0s stay correct.
  - (11)-(13) fix case-020 t0's dq-4: the availability-precondition AC is placed in Risks at decompose time, or flagged at FIRST review and moved by the unconditional first revise (phase-machine analysis: a PASSING re-review never triggers another revise — which is exactly how t0's minor soft-AC issue survived). Safe: the scan keys on "granted by parties outside the strategy"; corpus scan of every AC in all 33 trials shows the only such AC is the failing trial's own; passing trials' "available"-worded ACs are deliverable conditions, explicitly protected.
- Building on prior RESULTS: built directly on cand_0001's accepted validator + Step-8c-precondition + review-1.7 + revise wiring (its RESULT: ACCEPT, fixed case-015, broke nothing). No regressing edits to redesign — LEDGER `broke={}`. Did NOT re-try anything from rejected.jsonl (it is empty).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet (no rejected candidates in this run).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none — all 3 imperfect trials are addressed; if the gate still shows a flaky trial, read WHICH trial/judge moved: a dq-4 with a new "one minor gap" means the grader found a different gap than the three diagnosed here (the residual risk is grader-side inconsistency, as FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS notes for case-018 in iter 1).
- Plateau signal: val 0.982 with 3 flaky trials × 1 failing trial each — the remaining headroom is +0.018 (0.982→1.0). This iteration targets all of it with verified mechanisms; if the gate ACCEPTS but val stays ~0.98-0.99, the residual is per-trial LLM-grader variance (dq 4-vs-5 on borderline decompositions), not a fixable prompt defect — next lever would be raising the INTERNAL review's bar (more conservative AC/signal standards) only if a specific recurring gap shows up in the feedback.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective this run; detect_loop_patterns not applicable. The new validator check adds no model tokens (pure local Bash); the review-side checks add at most one extra revise cycle on the exact failing patterns (corpus-verified to not fire on passing trials).
- Focus next iteration: read the gate RESULT per-task. If case-013 still dips: check whether the validator ran at decompose time in the new trace (it should be a no-op now) and whether implementation_type_rules still appears. If case-014/020 still dip: read the dq rationale for a NEW "one minor gap" — do not re-diagnose the fixed ones; the grader names its gap explicitly. If everything holds at 1.0, the run is at ceiling — consider stopping or spending remaining iterations on robustness (e.g. the mandated-AC judge B9 will eventually gate; pre-adding Rules 24/25 AC-presence checks to the validator would be free preparation, but ONLY if a future RESULT shows it becoming REAL).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.992 Δ=+0.011 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={case-013-human-process-gates, case-014-tech-preview-foundation, case-020-hardware-dependent-investigation, case-030-real-operator-structured-logging} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0002: ACCEPTED val=0.992 Δ=+0.011 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — make the dq-5 recording shapes mandatory: re-split triggers for kept oversized epics + inline Step-4 bundling analysis in the matrix, plus revise-playbook split-wiring and stale-sweep rules
- Changes I made (1 line/edit; file + cluster):
  1. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8a Health Warnings — when an epic is kept above ~2 weeks as ONE logical change, record a concrete re-split trigger (cluster A / case-030 t0 size gap).
  2. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 3 — oversized-epic handling: monolith keeps the split demand; one-logical-change overage demands a re-split trigger (minor, named correction), never a terminal note or an un-actionable split suggestion; trigger present → watch item (cluster A).
  3. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — new playbook entry "oversized but one logical change": add the trigger, do NOT split (cluster A).
  4. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 4 — when keeping a lower-priority HLR bundled, record the priority-split analysis inline in the traceability matrix row (`bundled` + why not separately schedulable) (cluster B / case-030 t0 HLR-7 half-gap).
  5. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 1 — justified-bundling mirror case: analysis on the record (row flag or substantive note) = compliant; bare pointer/scattered/absent = minor "record it", never a split demand for a surface-sharing HLR (cluster B).
  6. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — new playbook entry "missing bundling analysis": add the row flag + rationale, do not re-split (cluster B).
  7. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — split-wiring rule (same-repo sub-deliverable split is parallel per Rule 15; enforcement/verification coupling is an AC gate, never an edge) + stale-structural-reference sweep of the summary after epic-structure changes (cluster C / the t0 E001→E004 edge churn + "all three epics" slip).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - (1)-(3) fix case-030 t0's dq-4 "one clear minor gap": the final internal review left E001's size as a terminal "noted for planning awareness only" note, and review #1's split suggestion (lint rule out) could not bring the epic under the guideline — the external grader docked exactly that ("the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked"). With the edits, the trigger lands at decompose time or is demanded at first review and added by the unconditional first revise — the shape the t2 grader quoted when scoring 5 ("records a concrete re-split trigger if the audit exceeds the 75% estimate. This is a defensible trade-off, not a monolith gap"). Expected case-030 mean 0.92 → ~1.0. Safe: BOUNDED — fires only on kept above-guideline epics; the 4 passing trials with size flags already write trigger-style conditionals in their review issues (case-019 t1 "if capacity-constrained", case-020 t1 "if the campaign outgrows a sprint", case-030 t1/t2), and case-029 t0's E005 monolith major (multiple work streams) is explicitly preserved by the monolith/one-logical-change discriminator.
  - (4)-(6) fix the second named half-gap (HLR-7 P1-into-P0 "not covered by a triage escape"): t0 recorded the bundling rationale as prose + a bare-pointer matrix footnote, while every dq-5 sibling and all 8 passing bundling trials (case-016 ×3, case-029 ×3, case-030 t1/t2) put the `bundled` flag with the not-separately-schedulable rationale in the matrix row itself — the exact language the t1/t2 graders repeated when scoring 5. With the edits the row flag is mandatory at decompose time and its absence is caught at FIRST review (where the unconditional revise can fix it). Safe: BOUNDED — verified per-trial that every passing bundling decomposition already produces the inline flag; the review accepts case-018 t2's substantive bundling note as well, so only the failing trial's bare-pointer shape is flagged (minor, no criterion zeroed).
  - (7) removes the two revise-time defects visible in the failing trace: the revise wired an E001→E004 edge no DAG rule creates (re-review: "unjustified blocking edge... No DAG rule creates it") and left "all three epics" stale after the 4-epic split (external grader: "cosmetic slip... stale text after the review-driven lint-rule split"). Safe: BOUNDED — fires only when the revise splits/restructures epics; case-029 t0's split edges (gated_by the design Investigation + builds-against the rendered Service surface) are exactly what the new wiring rule prescribes, so its passing outcome is unchanged.
- Building on prior RESULTS: built on cand_0001 + cand_0002's accepted review-calibration pattern (discriminating condition + first-review firing + unconditional-revise wiring + revise playbook entry) — applied this iteration to two NEW checks. LEDGER `broke={}` on both prior iterations, so nothing to redesign; rejected.jsonl is empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none (no rejected candidates in this run).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none diagnosed — this is the last imperfect trial of 33. Residual risk is grader-side variance on borderline dq 4-vs-5 judgment calls (this iteration makes the artifact shapes the graders reward mandatory, which is the strongest available lever against that variance). If case-030 still dips: read WHICH gap the grader names — a NEW gap means a different judgment call than the two recorded here; do not re-diagnose these.
- Plateau signal: val 0.992 with 1 flaky task × 1 failing trial — headroom is +0.008. Both prior RESULTs were ACCEPT with small positive Δ and empty broke/fixed sets (moves under 2·SE); this iteration targets the only remaining measured failure with a trace-verified mechanism. If the gate ACCEPTS and val reaches ~1.0, the run is at ceiling — remaining iterations should go to robustness prep (e.g. the mandated-AC Rules 24/25 validator checks, currently staged thresholdless) rather than more dq-calibration edits.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective this run; detect_loop_patterns not applicable. The edits add no model tokens at decompose time (one sentence in Health Warnings / the matrix row) and REMOVE a review+revise cycle on the failing shape (the un-actionable split suggestion that caused re-review churn in t0).
- Focus next iteration: read the gate RESULT per-task. If case-030 holds at 1.0, consider robustness-only iterations (mandated-AC validator prep) or stopping. If it dips, extract the grader's named gap from the new t0-equivalent trial and check whether the trigger/analysis landed in the artifact (the review-demand path only works if the first review fires the new checks — verify the review issues list contains the new correction text before redesigning anything).

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.958 Δ=-0.034 · fixed={—} · broke={—} · unresolved={case-013-human-process-gates, case-024-real-default-vector-store, case-030-real-operator-structured-logging} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — no task that was passing under the parent regressed: this batch did not clear the gate's threshold, it did not do damage. So the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign — re-measure with more trials in ONE evaluation, or make the effect bigger. Keep the edits that produced the `fixed` tasks above as your starting point; do not rewrite them on this round's numbers.

## Iteration cand_0005 — same cluster as cand_0003, different mechanism class: validator check 6 (overage triggers) + review Criterion-3 SCORING calibration, wired decompose→validator→review→revise
- Changes I made (1 line/edit; file + cluster):
  1. `scripts/validate_decomposition.py` — NEW check 6: a summary that acknowledges an epic above the ~2-week guideline must carry a re-split trigger; negation-guarded, summary-side, judge parity (cluster A / case-030 t0).
  2. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 6.5 — kept overages must record the re-split trigger in the Health Warning; bare "planning awareness" notes are named as the defect (cluster A).
  3. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8c — validator description + fix path extended to the summary (cluster A).
  4. `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 3 — SCORING calibration: one-logical-change overage WITH a recorded trigger = watch item, criterion may score 2; bare no-trigger note = 1 with named correction; un-actionable split suggestions forbidden for that shape; monolith split demand preserved (cluster A).
  5. `prompts/review-agent.md` Step 1.7 — check-6 violation → minor Epic-Boundaries issue that does NOT zero the criterion but reaches the unconditional revise (cluster A).
  6. `prompts/revise-agent.md` — playbook entry: oversized-but-one-logical-change → add the trigger, do NOT split (cluster A).
  7. `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 4 — bundling recorded as a `bundled` row flag + inline rationale in the HLR Traceability Matrix (cluster B / the grader's second named half-gap).
  8. `epic-decompose/SKILL.md` — description gains the "Use when" clause (removes the validation warning on cand_0003's rejection record; runner invokes by exact name, so no behavior change).
- Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe:
  - (1)-(6) fix case-030 t0's dq-4: the trigger lands at decompose time (Step 6.5 rule; check 6 as the mechanical precondition of `decompose_complete`), and if it ever doesn't, the first review flags it as a minor issue with a named correction that the unconditional revise applies. The internal review stops docking triggered overages — removing the "which the embedded adversarial review also docked" echo the external grader quoted — and stops issuing the split suggestion whose execution caused the t0 churn chain (split → overage remains → unjustified edge → failed re-review → stale counts). Expected case-030 mean 0.92 → ~1.0 (the t1/t2 shapes on the same facts scored 5/5 with 14/14 internal reviews). Safe: BOUNDED — corpus-verified end-to-end over all 33 reconstructed trials, check 6 fires on EXACTLY case-030 t0; only that trial's review ever docked for size; the trigger/watch-item handling is already what the passing reviews do (case-019 t1 "if capacity-constrained", case-020 t1 "if the campaign outgrows a sprint", case-030 t1/t2); case-029 t0's monolith split demand is explicitly preserved by the heterogeneous-work-stream discriminator.
  - (7) addresses the grader's second named half-gap (HLR-7 bundling "not covered by a triage escape"): the on-matrix `bundled` flag is the exact t1 row-shape the grader quoted at 5/5. Safe: BOUNDED to the bundling branch — the 15 corpus bundling trials' artifacts gain an additive, grader-praised flag; no judge consumes matrix cells mechanically; deliberately NO review-side demand, because the passing bundling trials (case-014/015/018/029) record analyses heterogeneously and a demand would churn them.
  - (8) is hygiene: zero behavioral surface.
- Building on prior RESULTS: built on cand_0001 + cand_0002's accepted validator/Step-8c-precondition/review-1.7/revise wiring (the bundled-script lever both ACCEPTs used) and on cand_0002's empty-`broke` record. cand_0003's RESULT (REJECTED, Δ −0.034, broke={}) showed its prose-mandate batch did no measurable damage but didn't clear the bar — per the framework note ("the lever is POWER or SIZE, not a redesign") I changed the MECHANISM class, not just the wording: the review edit now changes the scoring rule that produced "this criterion cannot score 2" (cand_0003 changed only the issue shape), the trigger requirement is mechanically enforced (cand_0003 had no validator change), the bundling fix is one convention sentence with no review/revise mirrors, and the stale-sweep rule is dropped. I did NOT re-try: the Step-8a Health-Warnings mandate wording, the review Criterion-1/3 mirror paragraphs, the revise split-wiring + stale-sweep rules (all in cand_0003's diff.patch). cand_0004's 0%-valid-score evaluation was an evaluation-infrastructure failure on an empty batch — nothing to avoid in the edit space, but it cost a slot; nothing in my batch touches infrastructure.
- Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test): none newly — cand_0003's RESULT did NOT refute the cluster's mechanism (broke={}, noise-dominated measurement; the note explicitly says "do not redesign on this round's numbers"), so the cluster stays live with a stronger mechanism. The one thing cand_0003's rejection DOES establish: a prose-only mandate batch on this cluster measured ≤ 0 against a 0.3·SE bar — prose alone is not enough power, which is exactly why this batch leans on the validator.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: none — this is the last imperfect trial of 33 (case-030 t0). Residual risk is grader-side dq 4-vs-5 variance on borderline judgment calls; this batch makes the two grader-quoted recording shapes (trigger, row flag) mandatory, which is the strongest available lever against that variance.
- Plateau signal: val 0.992, headroom +0.008 (one trial × one dq point = +0.0076) — below the gate's observed 0.3·SE bar (cand_0003's measurement had SE=0.033 → bar ≈ 0.01; cand_0002's ACCEPT cleared at Δ +0.011). Even a perfect fix of the last trial may land sub-bar depending on this evaluation's noise draw. If this batch is REJECTED with empty `broke` again, the honest read is measurement-limited-at-ceiling: re-measuring the same edit under a fresh tag is the only move that adds information — do NOT redesign the edits. If it ACCEPTs, val should read ~1.0 and remaining iterations should go to robustness prep only (e.g. mandated-AC Rules 24/25 validator checks if judge B9 ever goes live) or stopping.
- Cost-reduction opportunity: cost/latency is not a declared objective this run; detect_loop_patterns not applicable. Check 6 adds no model tokens (pure local Bash); edits (1)/(4)/(6) REMOVE a full review+revise+re-review cycle on the failing shape (the t0 churn chain) — net cheaper.
